title: @c15t/react-native: native consent for mobile
description: Private prerelease for React Native, Expo development builds and native iOS/Android integration. One native engine owns policy, durable choices and SDK gates before JavaScript starts. SwiftUI and Compose provide the shared stock consent screens.
features: Native Swift and Kotlin consent authority, durable records and synchronous SDK gates before JavaScript
Shared SwiftUI and Compose presenters with native drafts, IAB disclosures, search and standing preferences
Durable local commit outcomes and queued delivery, including offline withdrawal
Build-exported endpoint-bound policies for first-install offline prompts, with explicit authority expiry
Headless React Native hooks and commands, separate ATT authorization and app-owned native installation
prerequisites: React Native 0.86.x or 0.87.x with the New Architecture enabled
React 19.2.3 or later, below 19.3.0, to render the built-in components
A custom native build: Expo Go cannot load this package's native module, so use a development build
An Inth hosted project URL, such as https://your-project.inth.app. Advanced self-hosted deployments remain supported.
manualInstallation: This package is still `private: true`. Obtain the matching package tarball and native artifacts from the maintainer. Public npm, Maven and remote SwiftPM installation, cloud builds and device acceptance are not established by this checkout.

customSections.Native setup before JavaScript: Start with an Inth project and its authored policy. The reference apps use https://example-inth.inth.app/. Replace it with your own project URL. Configure the native launch hooks before optional SDK startup; `C15tProvider` attaches to that engine and checks the protocol. It does not bootstrap a JavaScript consent engine. Disable vendor automatic startup and keep gates current after withdrawal.
customSections.Local success and delivery: Check `CommitResult.ok` after `save`, `acceptAll` or `rejectAll`. A resolved promise can refuse a commit. `ok: true, queued: true` means durable local success; it does not prove backend delivery. Keep refused drafts and retry controls. Stock native presenter outcomes report durable commits separately from presentation and dismissal.

customSections.IAB and ads: Native IAB and Additional Consent APIs do not establish IAB registration, Google certification or AdMob interoperability. Vendor scope alone is not approved CMP configuration. ATT is a separate platform permission and never grants consent. Keep an ad integration disabled until its actual SDK, policy and certification requirements are verified.
customSections.Self-hosted and headless integration: Hosted Inth is the recommended starting point. The existing self-hosted transports, native installation APIs, React components and headless hooks remain available. Browser script-loader and CSS APIs are not native SDK gates.
